'''Marvin Chester''' (29 December 1930 in [[New York, New York]] – 22 April 2016) was a [[UCLA]] emeritus professor of [[Physics]] who specialized in [[quantum mechanics]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://chesters.org/marvin/obituary.html |title=The Obituary for Marvin Chester |website=chesters.org |access-date=2018-03-05}}</ref> After receiving his [[B.S.]] undergraduate degree from the [[City College of New York]] in 1952, he studied under [[Richard Feynman]] and [[John R. Pellam]] at [[California Institute of Technology]] where he received his [[Ph.D.]] in [[Physics]] in 1961. Thereafter he spent the following 31 years (1961 to 1992) as a faculty member in the [[Physics]] department at [[UCLA]].

==Physics==

Dr. Chester is perhaps best known for his text book for student physicists called ''Primer of Quantum Mechanics'' which connects the mathematical machinery of [[quantum mechanics]] directly to its philosophical underpinnings.<ref>{{cite book|last=Chester|first=Marvin|title=Primer of Quantum Mechanics|year=1987|publisher=Dover Publications, Inc.|location=Mineola, New York|isbn=978-0-486-42878-9}}</ref> 
 
Among his more substantial contributions to the field, he predicted and demonstrated a [[Bernoulli Effect]] in the electron gas.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Chester|first=Marvin|title=Evidence for a Configurational Emf in a Conducting Medium|journal=Physical Review Letters|date=1 August 1960|volume=5|issue=3|pages=91–93|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.5.91|bibcode=1960PhRvL...5...91C|url=https://authors.library.caltech.edu/7490/1/CHEprl60.pdf}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last=Chester|first=Marvin|title=Theory of a Configurational emf|journal=Physical Review|date=February 1964|volume=133|issue=4A|pages=A907–A915|doi=10.1103/PhysRev.133.A907|bibcode=1964PhRv..133..907C}}</ref> 
 
He is known for playing with and challenging the formal constructs of the scientific publication. One example of this can be found in ''An experiment regarding the wave function of superfluid helium''; A published technical description of an experiment to detect the [[diffraction]], because of its order parameter wave function property, of bulk [[superfluid helium]] flow through a grating - written in rhymed verse.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Chester|first=Marvin |author2=E. Guyon |author3=B.K. Jones |title=An experiment regarding the wave function of superfluid helium|journal=Solid State Communications|year=1967|volume=5|issue=10|pages=807–808|doi=10.1016/0038-1098(67)90713-2|bibcode=1967SSCom...5..807C }}</ref>

==Symmetry & Identity==

He showed that the notion of identity (identification) is connected to the concept of [[symmetry]]. He established the connection via the mathematical apparatus of [[group theory]], the abstract formulation of symmetry.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Chester|first=Marvin|title=Is symmetry identity?|journal=International Studies in the Philosophy of Science|date=July 2002|volume=16|issue=2|pages=111–124|doi=10.1080/02698590220145061|arxiv=1202.0292|s2cid=73612283}}</ref>

==Population Dynamics==

He proposed that the following statement is a fundamental principle governing nature: "The effect on the environment of a population’s success is to alter that environment in a way that opposes the success." By showing how to formulate it quantitatively he enabled the principle to be tested empirically in the laboratory.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Chester|first=Marvin|title=A Fundamental Principle Governing Populations|journal=Acta Biotheoretica|date=2012-09-01|volume=60|issue=3|pages=289–302|doi=10.1007/s10441-012-9160-6|pmid=22581491|s2cid=29842966}}</ref>
